1.title: Git, GitHub and the course map
1.text: Git, Git Hub and the course map. Git is a distributed version control system: it records the history of a project on your computer. Distributed means every clone holds the whole history, so you can commit, branch and read the log with no network. Git Hub is a service that hosts Git repositories and adds pull requests, issues and Actions. The figure is the course map.

1.title: Git, GitHub and the course map, continued
1.text: Git, Git Hub and the course map. What it is. Git: A tool that records history. Git Hub: A service that hosts repositories. Where it lives. Git: On your computer. Git Hub: On the web. Needs a network. Git: Only to share work. Git Hub: Yes. Gives you. Git: Commits, branches, merges. Git Hub: Pull requests, issues, Actions. Works alone. Git: Yes. Git Hub: No, it hosts Git repositories. Tip: Git works without Git Hub, but Git Hub does not work without Git. Learn the Git model first: every Git Hub feature is built on it.

1.title: Install check and first-time configuration
1.text: Install check and first-time configuration. Check the install with git the version flag. Use Git two point two eight or later: the course uses git init dash b main, git switch and git restore. The lab used Git two point five zero.one. In this course, the lab means the practice repositories built for the examples: every command shown was run there, and the output you see is real. Git writes your name and email into every commit, so set them once. Do every Try it block in a sandbox folder, a throw-away place where no real project can be harmed.

1.text: Install check and first-time configuration. user dot name. What it controls: Name stored in each commit. Typical value: Ada Lovelace. user dot email. What it controls: Email stored in each commit. Typical value: Your own address. init dot default Branch. What it controls: First branch of new repositories. Typical value: main. core dot editor. What it controls: Program that opens for messages. Typical value: nano or your editor. On your own machine you set these once for every repository, for instance git config the global flag user dot name. The Try it blocks use the local flag so that the settings stay inside the sandbox repository.

1.title: Configuration levels and line endings
1.text: Configuration levels and line endings. Git reads settings from three files, and the most specific level wins. System. Flag: the system flag. Applies to: Every user of the computer. Stored in: The Git install folder. Global. Flag: the global flag. Applies to: You, in every repository. Stored in: dot gitconfig in your home folder. Local. Flag: the local flag. Applies to: One repository. Stored in: dot git slash config.

1.title: Configuration levels and line endings, continued
1.text: Configuration levels and line endings. git config the list flag the show origin flag prints every setting and its file. Add the show scope flag to see the level too. git config the get flag user dot name prints the winning value, and the unset flag removes a setting. The output below comes from a lab where all three levels set the same key. On your machine you will usually see global and local lines only.

1.title: Configuration levels and line endings, continued
1.text: Configuration levels and line endings. Line endings differ by system: Windows ends lines with C R L F, mac O S and Linux with L F. Mixed endings make every line look changed in a diff. core dot autocrlf is a personal setting, and the Windows installer defaults to converting. autocrlf true. On commit: C R L F becomes L F. On checkout: L F becomes C R L F. autocrlf input. On commit: C R L F becomes L F. On checkout: Nothing changes. autocrlf false. On commit: Nothing changes. On checkout: Nothing changes. With true, Git warns that L F will be replaced by C R L F the next time it touches a file.

1.title: Configuration levels and line endings, continued
1.text: Configuration levels and line endings. The team-wide answer is a dot gitattributes file in the repository. The line text auto stores text files with L F for everyone who clones, whatever their personal setting. A line such as dot sh text eol lf keeps L F in the working tree too, which shell scripts need on Windows. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

2.title: First repository, status and help
2.text: First repository, status and help. git init dash b main creates the hidden dot git folder and names the first branch. Without dash b, the name comes from init dot default Branch, and with neither, Git two point five zero.one still starts on master. The dash b flag wins over the setting. git status is the command you will run most. In the new repository it says On branch main, No commits yet and nothing to commit, and it suggests the next step when files appear. Tip: Start every repository with git init dash b main. The branch name then never depends on one computer's settings.

2.title: First repository, status and help, continued
2.text: First repository, status and help. Help is built in. git help status. The full manual page. git status dash h. A short usage summary in the terminal. git help dash a. Every available command. git help dash g. Concept guides such as everyday and glossary.

2.title: Practice Question 1
2.text: Question one. Ada's new laptop has no Git identity yet. She wants every repository she creates on it to record her name and email. What should she run? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: git config the global flag for the name and email, once on the laptop. The global level applies to your user in every repository, so one setting covers all of Ada's future repositories.

2.title: Practice Question 2
2.text: Question two. The config listing shows global... user dot name Global Gina and local file dot git slash config user dot name Ada Lovelace. Which name is stored in the next commit made in this repository? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Ada Lovelace, because the local level wins over the global level. The most specific level wins, and the local level is the most specific.

2.title: Practice Question 3
2.text: Question three. Bob runs git init in a new folder on a computer with no Git settings. git status says "On branch master", but his team uses main. Which command would have started on main? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: git init dash b main. The dash b flag names the first branch and wins over any setting.

2.title: Practice Question 4
2.text: Question four. A team works on Windows and Linux. Diffs show every line changed in files that a Windows developer touched. What is the most reliable fix for the whole team? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Add a dot gitattributes file with text auto and commit it to the repository. A committed dot gitattributes travels with the repository, so every clone gets the same rule whatever the personal settings.

2.title: Practice Question 5
2.text: Question five. Cy runs git status in a folder he just initialized. It prints "On branch main", "No commits yet" and "nothing to commit". What does this tell him? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: The repository exists, has no history yet and has no files to record. This is the normal state of a new empty repository, not an error.

2.title: Practice Question 6
2.text: Question six. Cy is on a train with no network. In his existing clone, which task can he still do completely? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Commit changes, create branches and read the project history. Git is distributed: every clone holds the whole history, while pull requests, issues and Actions need Git Hub.

2.title: Recall Check 1
2.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What does "distributed" mean for Git? Answer: Every clone holds the whole history of the project. Question two. Which command lists every setting and the file it comes from? Answer: git config the list flag the show origin flag. Question three. Which configuration level wins when a key is set at several levels? Answer: The most specific one: local.

2.title: Recall Check 2
2.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Which command creates a repository whose first branch is main? Answer: git init dash b main. Question five. Name two things Git Hub adds around Git. Answer: Any two of pull requests, issues and Actions. Question six. Which command prints a short usage summary of git status in the terminal? Answer: git status dash h.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. Git and Git Hub: Git records history on your computer. Install check: git the version flag; use two point two eight or later. Identity: user dot name and user dot email go into every commit. Levels: system, global, local; the most specific wins. Inspect: git config the list flag the show origin flag, add the show scope flag for the level. Line endings: autocrlf true, input, false; share the rule with dot gitattributes and text auto. First repository: git init dash b main, then git status. Help: git help, git status dash h, git help dash a, git help dash g. Practice: Work in a sandbox folder and use the local flag settings.
